headline: DC has an official beat, and the Wizards have barely touched it.
summary: Washington's sound is go-go, the nonstop percussion funk Chuck Brown built in the 1970s, still played from Southeast to Prince George's County. DC also invented hardcore and the Quiet Storm. The team's music ties are mostly fan-made, so the Dybantsa era can sound like DC on purpose. Make go-go product with the people who keep it alive, and pay them, and skip the hardcore pastiche that has burned Nike before.

insights.title: Go-go is the law here, won as a protest
insights.detail: In April 2019, a cellphone store at 7th Street and Florida Avenue NW in Shaw was told to turn off the go-go it had played onto the sidewalk for years. A resident of a new luxury building had complained. #DontMuteDC rallies and the Moechella street concerts at 14th and U got the music back on within days. In February 2020 the Council and Mayor Bowser made go-go the official music of the District.
insights.implication: Go-go product reads as civic pride and an anti-displacement statement at once. Co-create it with the bands and organizers who won that fight, credit them and pay them. Launch in Shaw or Anacostia, not at a downtown-only theme night.

insights.title: The beat never stops
insights.detail: Chuck Brown designed go-go as one continuous set, with no gaps between songs. Congas, cowbell, roto-toms and timbales hold it together. A lead talker trades chants with the crowd ('Wind me up, Chuck!') and shouts out neighborhoods and crews. Bounce beat, the faster offshoot that took over younger crowds in the 2000s, kept the same engine.
insights.implication: Design for rhythm and roll call: percussion hardware details, chant typography and neighborhood shout-out graphics. Pair the product with a live pocket band (congas, cowbell, roto-toms) at timeouts, as the Wizards' sonic signature.

insights.title: Day-glo Globe posters set the look
insights.detail: For decades, go-go, R&B and soul shows across the DMV were advertised with Baltimore's Globe Poster prints. Fluorescent split-fountain gradients (yellow bleeding into orange and pink) sat under stacked wood-type headlines, stapled to poles and storefronts. MICA acquired Globe's archive of type, blocks and posters in 2011 and prints from it.
insights.implication: Make a Globe-style Wizards gig-poster series, printed from the original type with MICA, numbered and dated per game. It gives Nike a real graphic system and a collectible insert for city product.

insights.title: DC also invented hardcore and the Quiet Storm
insights.detail: Bad Brains, Minor Threat ('Straight Edge,' 1981) and Ian MacKaye's Dischord Records made DC the capital of DIY hardcore. In 1976, Howard University's WHUR 96.3 and student DJ Melvin Lindsey created the Quiet Storm late-night R&B format.
insights.implication: The Quiet Storm is an open lane for a plush, late-night capsule co-branded with WHUR under license. Hardcore is closed. Nike SB's 2005 'Major Threat' tour poster copied Minor Threat's record cover, and Nike had to apologize to Dischord.

insights.title: The modern sound is R&B-forward, and says DMV
insights.detail: Ari Lennox (DC, Dreamville), Brent Faiyaz (Columbia, Md.), GoldLink, Wale, Shy Glizzy and Rico Nasty define the current sound. Shy Glizzy is from Southeast, Rico Nasty from Prince George's County. GoldLink's 2017 'At What Cost' is a go-go-soaked DC concept album. Fans claim all of it as the DMV.
insights.implication: Cast collaborators across DC, PG County and Northern Virginia, and screen each for footwear conflicts. GoldLink and Wale both put go-go inside rap, so they are the natural bridge between heritage and now.

insights.title: The team's music link is fan-made. The reset can fix that
insights.detail: Wale is the most visible celebrity Wizards fan, and he built early hits on go-go (including his 2009 hit 'Pretty Girls'). DJ Kool's DC party record 'Let Me Clear My Throat' (1996) is an arena-playlist staple. Go-go has filled the franchise's arena before: the 1980s 'Go-Go Live at the Capital Centre' recordings were made in the Bullets' Landover home.
insights.implication: After a 17-65 season and a 2023-24 near-move to Virginia, make the Dybantsa, Young and Davis era sound like the District. Build a go-go walkout and timeout identity, a launch content series with DC artists, and product that plants the team in DC. Trae Young is an adidas athlete, so use him only through NBA-licensed assets.

places.name: Howard Theatre
places.why: Opened in 1910 as a flagship Black theater (Duke Ellington, Ella Fitzgerald) and restored in 2012. It is the right room for a go-go launch show.

places.name: 7th Street & Florida Avenue NW
places.why: A store's sidewalk go-go was switched off here in 2019, which sparked #DontMuteDC. Start any go-go product story by acknowledging it.

places.name: Chuck Brown Memorial Park
places.why: The city's memorial to the Godfather of Go-Go, opened in 2014. It is the natural gathering point on Chuck Brown Day.

places.name: Howard University: The Yard and WHUR 96.3
places.why: Howard's commercial station invented the Quiet Storm. Yardfest on The Yard is DC's biggest homecoming concert each October.

places.name: Anacostia (Martin Luther King Jr. Ave SE)
places.why: Southeast's main street, next to Barry Farm, where Junkyard Band started on buckets and trash cans. It is go-go's heartland, and a place where city product should actually be sold.

places.name: 9:30 Club
places.why: Born in 1980 on F Street in the punk era, now DC's flagship mid-size club. I.M.P. runs it alongside The Atlantis next door and The Anthem.

places.name: The Anthem
places.why: A 6,000-capacity hall that opened in 2017, big enough for a city-product launch concert with go-go and DMV rap on one bill.

places.name: Som Records
places.why: A used-vinyl shop strong in soul, funk and jazz, where DC's crate-diggers and DJs shop.

places.name: Joe's Record Paradise
places.why: A crate-digger institution since the 1970s. It sits just over the line in Montgomery County, proof that the scene's map is the DMV.

people.name: Chuck Brown (1936-2012)
people.role: Guitarist and bandleader of Chuck Brown & the Soul Searchers; the Godfather of Go-Go
people.why: 'Bustin' Loose' (1978) and the call 'Wind me up, Chuck!' are the root of the city's sound. His estate owns his name, likeness and catalog.

people.name: Rare Essence
people.why: The genre's longest-running working band, and the default booking for any real go-go night.

people.name: Backyard Band
people.role: Go-go band led by Anwan 'Big G' Glover
people.why: Leaders of the harder, rap-leaning go-go that fed bounce beat. Glover is also known as Slim Charles on 'The Wire.'

people.name: Junkyard Band
people.role: Go-go band from Barry Farm in Southeast
people.why: Started as kids drumming on buckets and scrap, and signed to Def Jam in the 1980s. That origin story suits youth-hoops or community product.

people.name: Wale
people.role: DC rapper who built his early career on go-go
people.why: The most visible celebrity Wizards fan, with go-go woven through his catalog. Check his current endorsement deals before approaching him.

people.name: GoldLink
people.why: His 2017 album 'At What Cost' is a go-go-soaked portrait of DC. Its single 'Crew' (with Brent Faiyaz and Shy Glizzy) is a modern DMV anthem.

people.name: DJ Kool
people.why: 'Let Me Clear My Throat' (1996), a party record bred in DC's go-go clubs, plays in arenas everywhere. DC already soundtracks sports nationally.

people.name: #DontMuteDC organizers (Ronald Moten's Don't Mute DC; Long Live GoGo)
people.role: Go-go advocacy groups behind the 2019 protests, the Moechella street concerts and the official-music campaign
people.why: They won go-go's legal status. They can vet, co-host and credibly endorse any go-go launch.

moments.name: Wizards home opener: Dybantsa's first home game
moments.why: The first home look at the new era is the moment to debut a go-go sonic identity and the first city-product drop.

moments.name: Howard University Homecoming and Yardfest
moments.why: DC's biggest Black homecoming and its free concert on The Yard land right at tipoff. Good timing for a Quiet Storm or DMV-artist drop.

moments.name: Go-go's official-music anniversary and Black History Month
moments.timing: February (the law was signed in February 2020)
moments.why: A mid-season window for a go-go heritage night with Rare Essence or Backyard Band, and a capsule that credits #DontMuteDC.

moments.name: National Cherry Blossom Festival and Petalpalooza
moments.timing: Late March to mid-April; Petalpalooza is usually an early-April Saturday
moments.why: The festival's free music-and-fireworks day lines up with the revived cherry-blossom City Edition and the regular season's last push.

moments.name: DC Emancipation Day
moments.why: A DC-only holiday marking the 1862 end of slavery in the District, celebrated with a parade and concerts during the final home stretch.

moments.name: Chuck Brown Day
moments.why: The city's go-go holiday. Aug 22, 2026 has passed, so August 2027 is the window to seed a roll-call or go-go capsule for the 2027-28 launch.

moments.name: DC JazzFest
moments.timing: Late August into Labor Day weekend, centered on The Wharf
moments.why: Duke Ellington's hometown festival gives summer reach on the waterfront, next to The Anthem.

vocabulary.meaning: The steady, swung go-go groove of conga, cowbell and kick. It runs under every song and never stops.
What a go-go band does when it's hitting hard ('RE was crankin' last night').
A live soundboard recording of a go-go show, sold on cassette and later CD and online. It is how the songs spread.
The faster, harder go-go style that took over younger crowds in the 2000s.
DC's go-go footwork dance, battled by crews.
DC for friend or bro ('what's up, moe'). It also gave Moechella its name.
DC's all-purpose word for a thing, place or song ('that jont is crankin'').
DC's nickname from its Black-majority era, taken national by Parliament's 1975 album of the same name.

designCues.cue: Globe split-fountain day-glo yellow fading to hot orange and pink
designCues.source: The fluorescent gradient backgrounds of Globe Poster prints that advertised DMV go-go shows.
designCues.use: Use it as a gradient panel or sublimated fade on warmups, hangtags and poster inserts. The hex approximates fluorescent ink, so match it with a neon lab dip.

designCues.cue: Wizards navy as the poster's headline ink
designCues.source: Globe posters set dark headlines over day-glo grounds. Team navy replaces the usual black.
designCues.use: Run navy wood-type over the yellow fade so the go-go system reads as Wizards. Confirm the value against the team's brand guide.

designCues.cue: Stacked wood-type headlines: heavy condensed gothic caps with worn letterpress edges
designCues.source: The Globe Poster type archive, now held and printed by MICA.
designCues.use: Set game dates, opponents and band-style lineups ('DYBANTSA • YOUNG • DAVIS') in licensed or MICA-printed Globe type. Don't fake it with a stock font.

designCues.cue: The go-go percussion kit: congas, cowbell, roto-toms, timbales
designCues.source: The instruments that hold the pocket in every go-go band.
designCues.use: Try cowbell-shaped zipper pulls and aglets, concentric roto-tom rings as a tonal emboss, and conga line art on sleeves.

designCues.cue: PA tape J-card: handwritten band, venue and date
designCues.source: The cassette inserts of live go-go recordings that circulated hand to hand.
designCues.use: Print a J-card-style label inside collars and on hangtags, dated to the specific home game, with a QR code to a commissioned live recording.

designCues.cue: Roll-call text wall: repeating all-caps neighborhood shout-outs
designCues.source: The lead talker's shout-outs to neighborhoods and crews in a go-go set.
designCues.use: Write the list with a working go-go lead talker and community input (Southeast, Uptown, PG, NoVA and so on). Leave out crew names that could carry beef.

designCues.cue: Don't Mute DC: the music that would not be turned down
designCues.source: The 2019 Shaw protests that made go-go DC's official music in 2020.
designCues.use: Make it the narrative anchor for a go-go capsule. Credit the organizers and share revenue with go-go youth music programs.

productHooks: An 'Official Music of DC' warmup and shooting shirt: a Globe-yellow fade into Wizards navy, with wood-type headlines printed with MICA. Co-design it with go-go bands and #DontMuteDC organizers, and launch it at a Rare Essence or Backyard Band show at the Howard Theatre around the home opener.
A 'PA Tape' tee series with J-card graphics dated to marquee home games. Each carries a download code for a commissioned live go-go recording. Sell it at Som Records and Joe's Record Paradise.
A 'Roll Call' hoodie of neighborhood shout-outs written with a go-go lead talker. Seed it on Chuck Brown Day (Aug 22) at Chuck Brown Memorial Park, with the estate's approval for any Chuck reference.
A 'Quiet Storm' late-night capsule in plush velour and fleece, co-branded with WHUR under license and released for Howard Homecoming in October.
A go-go stage at Petalpalooza in early April, paired with the revived cherry-blossom City Edition and a limited go-go-poster tee for the regular season's final push.
watchouts: Brand conflicts: Trae Young is an adidas signature athlete, so use him only through NBA-licensed assets. Confirm AJ Dybantsa's and Anthony Davis's deals. Screen Wale, GoldLink, Ari Lennox and Brent Faiyaz before any collaboration.

Nike's own history: the 2005 Nike SB 'Major Threat' poster copied Minor Threat's cover and drew a public apology. DC punk's anti-corporate ethic (Fugazi famously sold no merch) rules out hardcore, straight-edge or X-on-hand pastiche.

Go-go is Black DC's music and a symbol against displacement, with a long history of venue closures and police scrutiny of shows. Partner with the bands and organizers, credit them and pay them. Don't sell a sanitized 'go-go night' while development pushes its community out.

Licensing: clear the Chuck Brown estate (name, likeness, 'Bustin' Loose,' 'Wind me up, Chuck!'), MICA's Globe archive, and WHUR and Howard marks. Clear DJ Kool's record and its samples, band names, and Parliament's 'Chocolate City' album art. The nickname is public. The artwork is not.
The cherry trees were a 1912 gift from Tokyo. Keep cherry-blossom product botanical and DC-rooted. Avoid Japanese pastiche such as faux kanji, geisha imagery or rising-sun rays.
